sources.title: Entry into Niger
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Nigeriens Abroad
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Ministry of Foreign Affairs .gouv.ne service page sets Niger's entry, visa, transit and exceptional point-of-entry-authorization rules.
sources.supportingExcerpt: tous les étrangers ... sont tenus de présenter ... un visa nigérien, sauf en cas d’exemption prévue par un accord bilatéral ou communautaire.

sources.title: AES space: no visa for ECOWAS nationals
sources.officialityEvidence: The live official Niger press agency states it is the country's official press agency and reproduces the 14 December 2024 declaration by the AES Heads of State, including Niger's President.
sources.supportingExcerpt: les ressortissants de la CEDEAO n’ont pas besoin de visa pour entrer ... dans l’espace de la Confédération.

sources.title: ECOWAS statement on continued West African free movement after AES withdrawal
sources.jurisdiction: Economic Community of West African States
sources.officialityEvidence: The current ECOWAS Commission site reports the Commission President's 31 July 2025 statement that ECOWAS and the three AES countries agreed continuing regional free movement pending a new agreement.
sources.supportingExcerpt: until a new agreement is reached, the people of West Africa will continue to benefit ... particularly ... free movement.

sources.title: ECOWAS creation history and current member states
sources.jurisdiction: Economic Community of West African States
sources.officialityEvidence: The current ECOWAS Commission page names the 12 current members and records the 29 January 2025 withdrawal of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, permitting precise mapping of the declaration's former 15-member cohort.
sources.supportingExcerpt: On January 29, 2025, Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger officially withdrew from ECOWAS.

policies.title: ECOWAS ordinary passports: visa-free entry to Niger under AES declaration
policies.summary: The AES Heads of State declared that ECOWAS nationals need no visa to enter the AES space, which includes Niger. ECOWAS later reported that its members and the three AES States agreed continuing free movement pending a new agreement.
conditions: Applies only to nationals of the named ECOWAS State passport issuers holding ordinary passports for the normal visitor baseline.
AES States retain power, under national law, to refuse entry to ECOWAS nationals falling within inadmissible-immigrant categories.

The current MFA rule treats airport transit without leaving airport limits separately, and only permits a point-of-entry visa exceptionally on Interior Minister authorization for a person departing a country without a Niger mission; neither is a nationality-wide visitor route.

This policy does not decide residence administration, employment, commercial vehicle, diplomatic, official/service, refugee, laissez-passer, special-document, health, security or individual-admissibility treatment.
